## Story Goal

Expose the supporting tools of an agent's daily work as first-class APIs so the agent workspace screen can be built against one backend contract:

1. **Tasks & reminders** — an owner, an optional ticket link, a due instant, a state, and an append-only history. Overdue items are queryable through the standard collection query.
2. **Reminder firing** — reminders fire through the shared notification service. When a reminder is expressed in *working time*, its due instant is resolved against the branch calendar.
3. **Quick replies** — reusable reply bodies in **personal** and **shared** scopes, bilingual (en/ar), with server-side placeholder resolution for customer name, ticket reference and agent name.
4. **Mentions** — an agent can mention a colleague on an **internal note**; the mention notifies the mentioned user and grants them visibility only where permissions already allow it.
5. **Watchers** — any permitted user can watch/unwatch a ticket they do not own, and watchers receive the configured update notifications.
6. **No leakage** — none of these surfaces expose internal notes, mentions, or watch state to customer-facing endpoints.

**Out of scope:** frontend/workspace UI, recurring/repeating tasks, calendar (ICS) export, quick-reply approval workflows, and any change to the notification channel transports themselves.

## Product rules (from story)

| Area | Current behaviour | New behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Agent to-dos | No task/reminder concept exists in the codebase. | Tasks with owner, optional ticket link, due instant, state, and append-only history. Overdue is a queryable filter. |
| Reminder delivery | Only SLA/ticket events raise notifications. | A due reminder raises a notification through `NotificationDispatcher`. |
| Working-time due dates | `WorkingTimeService` is used by SLA only. | Reminders flagged as working-time resolve their due instant through the branch calendar. |
| Canned replies | Agents retype bodies. | Personal + shared quick replies, bilingual, with server-side placeholder resolution. |
| Pulling in a colleague | Assign or transfer only. | Mention a colleague on an internal note; mention notifies without changing assignment. |
| Following a ticket | Only assignee/participants get updates. | Any permitted user can watch/unwatch; watchers get configured updates. |

### 4 — Reminder firing through the shared notification service

**File:** `app/Domains/Notifications/Enums/NotificationEventType.php` — add cases: `AgentTaskReminder`, `TicketMentioned`, `TicketWatchedUpdate`. Keep the existing backing-value naming convention (grep the file for the existing cases before choosing strings).

**Create file:** `app/Domains/Notifications/Events/AgentTaskReminderNotification.php` — implements `NotifiableEvent`, copying the structure of `app/Domains/Notifications/Events/TicketAssignedNotification.php`. Payload: task uuid, title, due instant, optional ticket reference.

**File:** `database/seeders/NotificationTemplatesSeeder.php` — add **en + ar** templates for all three new event types. Missing templates throw `NotificationTemplateMissingException` at dispatch. The seeder must stay idempotent (`tests/Feature/Seeders/DatabaseSeederIdempotencyTest.php` re-runs it).

**Create file:** `app/Console/Commands/AgentTaskReminderSweepCommand.php`
- Model it on `app/Console/Commands/SlaSweepCommand.php`: a thin command that delegates to a service, bounded batch size, no inline time arithmetic.
- Selects tasks where `reminder_at <= now()`, `reminder_sent_at is null`, `state in (open, in_progress)`.
- For each: dispatch `AgentTaskReminderNotification` via `NotificationDispatcher`, stamp `reminder_sent_at`, record an `AgentTaskEvent` of type `ReminderFired`.
- **Idempotency:** stamp `reminder_sent_at` inside the same transaction as the dispatch so a crashed sweep cannot double-notify.
- Register the schedule in `routes/console.php` next to the existing sweeps.

**Working-time rule:** when `due_in_working_time` is true, the *stored* `reminder_at` is already the calendar-resolved absolute instant (resolved at write time by `ScheduleAgentTaskReminder`). The sweep does **no** calendar maths — it only compares instants. This keeps `tests/Unit/Sla/NoDirectTimeArithmeticTest.php` satisfied and makes the sweep cheap.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Task with no due date.** `due_at` is nullable; such a task is never overdue and is never picked up by the sweep. Enforced by the `null` guard in `AgentTask::scopeOverdue` and by the `reminder_at is not null` predicate in `AgentTaskReminderSweepCommand`.
- **Working-time reminder with no branch calendar.** When `branch_id` is null and the owner has no primary branch, fall back to storing the raw instant and record an `AgentTaskEvent` noting the fallback. **Do not** throw — a missing calendar must not block task creation.
- **Working-time reminder landing on a holiday.** `WorkingTimeService` must shift it to the next working instant. Verify with `tests/Unit/Organisation/WorkingTimeServiceTest.php` semantics before relying on a method.
- **Sweep runs twice concurrently.** Two workers could both select the same due task. Guard by stamping `reminder_sent_at` with a conditional update (`where reminder_sent_at is null`) and only dispatching when the update affected a row.
- **Task owner deactivated or anonymised.** `app/Domains/Security/Actions/DeactivateUser.php` and `AnonymisePersonalData.php` must not break on tasks. Open tasks owned by a deactivated user stay queryable by supervisors; the reminder sweep **skips** tasks whose owner is inactive rather than dispatching to a dead account.
- **Mentioning a user who cannot see the ticket.** Raises `MentionTargetNotVisibleException`; the whole message post rolls back. **Access is never granted by mentioning.**
- **Mention on a public reply.** Raises `MentionNotAllowedOnPublicReplyException`. This is the primary leakage guard — a customer-visible message must never carry mention metadata.
- **Self-mention.** Recorded in the pivot but produces **no** notification.
- **Duplicate mentions in one request.** De-duplicated before insert; the unique index on `(ticket_message_id, mentioned_user_id)` is the backstop.
- **Watching an already-watched ticket.** Idempotent success (unique index), not a 409.
- **Watcher loses ticket access later** (department transfer, role change, scope narrowing). Recipient resolution in `NotificationDispatcher` must re-check visibility at dispatch time via `NotificationPayloadAuthoriser` — a stale `ticket_watchers` row must not deliver content the user can no longer see.
- **Ticket merged or split.** `app/Domains/Ticketing/Actions/MergeTickets.php` — watchers of the source ticket should be carried to the target via a new merge relation under `app/Domains/Ticketing/Services/Merge/Relations/`, mirroring `TagMergeRelation.php`. Duplicate watch rows collapse on the unique index. `SplitTicket.php` does **not** copy watchers.
- **Quick reply with unmatched placeholder braces** (e.g. `{{customer_name`) — left verbatim; the renderer never throws on malformed input.
- **Quick reply rendered without a ticket.** Ticket placeholders resolve to an empty string, not the literal token.
- **Arabic / RTL and unicode in quick reply bodies and task titles.** Storage and rendering must be byte-safe; use `mb_*` functions in the renderer. See `app/Domains/Customers/Services/ArabicTextNormaliser.php` for precedent on unicode handling in this codebase.
- **Missing notification template for a new event type.** Throws `NotificationTemplateMissingException` at dispatch. Seeding en+ar templates in `NotificationTemplatesSeeder.php` is **not optional**.
- **Half-applied migration state.** The five migrations are independent; running only some leaves the API partially functional but never corrupts data. All FKs to `tickets`/`users` are declared with cascade or nullable semantics so a rollback cannot orphan rows.

Watch a ticket you do not own; watch twice is idempotent; unwatch a ticket you never watched returns the mapped error; a watcher receives a configured event and does **not** receive an internal-note event; the queue `watched=true` filter returns exactly the watched set.

## Migration / Rollback

- Five additive migrations; **no** existing table is altered destructively. `Ticket` and `TicketMessage` gain relations only, not columns.
- **Order matters:** `agent_tasks` before `agent_task_events`; `ticket_messages` and `tickets` already exist, so watcher/mention tables can run in any order after them.
- **Rollback:** each migration's `down()` drops only its own table. Rolling back all five removes the workspace surface entirely; the ticketing and notification domains keep working because every touch point (`TicketResource`, `TicketMessageResource`, `NotificationDispatcher`) treats watchers/mentions as **optional** relations.
- **Half-applied risk:** if `agent_tasks` exists but `agent_task_events` does not, task creation fails at the history write. Because every action wraps its write **and** its event append in one transaction, no task row survives without its `Created` event.
- New `NotificationEventType` cases with un-seeded templates throw at dispatch. **Run `php artisan db:seed --class=NotificationTemplatesSeeder` as part of the deploy** before enabling the reminder sweep schedule.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend static analysis:** run `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` from the repository root (config at `phpstan.neon`). Zero new errors.
2. **Migrations apply cleanly:** `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed` from the repository root. Confirm the seeders stay idempotent by running `php artisan db:seed` a second time.
3. **Backend unit tests:** `php artisan test --testsuite=Unit` (suites declared in `phpunit.xml`).
4. **Backend feature tests:** `php artisan test --testsuite=Feature`.
5. **Targeted runs:** `php artisan test tests/Feature/Workspace tests/Feature/Ticketing/TicketMentionTest.php tests/Feature/Ticketing/TicketWatcherTest.php`.
6. **Regression:** `php artisan test tests/Unit/Support tests/Feature/Api tests/Feature/Security` — the structural guard suites must stay green.
7. **Reminder sweep smoke:** create a task with `reminder_at` in the past, run the sweep command via `php artisan` (use the signature you registered), confirm exactly one notification row is created and a second run creates none.
8. **Leakage smoke:** hit the customer-facing ticket endpoints (the group guarded by `ProtectPublicEndpoint` in `routes/api.php`) for a ticket that has watchers and a mentioned internal note; assert the response body contains none of `mentions`, `watchers`, `is_watched`.
9. **Convenience:** check `Makefile` for an aggregate target and prefer it if one already runs lint + tests together.

## Done Criteria

- [x] Tasks have an owner, an optional ticket link, a due instant, a state, and an append-only event history exposed through the API.
- [x] Overdue tasks are queryable through a single `overdue` filter backed by one shared scope definition.
- [x] Reminders fire through `NotificationDispatcher` — no bespoke mail/queue path — and are idempotent across repeated sweeps.
- [x] Working-time reminders are resolved against the branch calendar via `WorkingTimeService`, with a safe fallback when no calendar exists.
- [x] Quick replies exist in `personal` and `shared` scopes, are bilingual (en + ar), and resolve `{{customer_name}}`, `{{ticket_reference}}` and `{{agent_name}}` **server-side**.
- [x] An agent can mention a colleague on an **internal note**; the mention notifies and never grants access the mentioned user did not already have.
- [x] Mentions on public replies are rejected with a mapped, localised error code.
- [x] Any permitted user can watch/unwatch a ticket they do not own; watch is idempotent; watchers receive only the configured event types.
- [x] Customer-facing endpoints expose **no** internal notes, mentions, watchers, or watch state — asserted by an explicit regression test.
- [x] New permission keys are in `PermissionKey.php`, granted in `PermissionsAndRolesSeeder.php`, and the catalogue tests pass.
- [x] New error codes have entries in **both** `lang/en/errors.php` and `lang/ar/errors.php`.
- [x] New notification event types have en + ar templates seeded idempotently.
- [x] Terminal tasks are covered by a registered retention purge handler.
- [x] `phpstan` and the full `Unit` + `Feature` suites are green.
